body.en: California governor calls for national tax on super-wealthy and suggests the US should own a stake in AI companies US politics live – latest updates California’s governor, Gavin Newsom , called for a national “billionaires tax” on Friday as he fights a ballot measure targeting the ultra-wealthy in his home state. Newsom, who is expected to run for president in 2028, published his proposal the day after California officials certified a ballot measure to levy a one-time 5% tax on residents worth more than $1bn. title.en: Utah governor orders ban on fireworks as wildfires rage across state

summary.en: Utah Governor Spencer Cox has declared a state of emergency and issued a temporary ban on personal fireworks until July 5th, as raging wildfires across the state have prompted evacuations and red-flag warnings.

body.en: Fireworks prohibition comes alongside state of emergency as wildfires prompt evacuations and red-flag warnings Utah governor Spencer Cox has announced a state of emergency and accompanying temporary prohibition on the use of personal fireworks until 5 July. The announcement comes as the state experiences an unprecedented wildfire season with blazes that have prompted evacuations in Eureka, a small town about 80 miles south of Salt Lake City. Under the governor’s executive order, the state forester is allowed to ban the use of fireworks anywhere in the state. The order temporarily suspends a 2024 law that disallowed the forester from banning fireworks in cities across the state. Continue reading...

title.en: US strikes Iran in response to cargo ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz, straining peace deal
title.zh: 美国打击伊朗，回应霍尔木兹海峡货船遇袭事件，和平协议陷入紧张

summary.en: Iran has also warned Gulf states not to side with the US as friction starts up again.

body.en:
The United States has attacked Iran on Friday in response to an Iranian drone strike on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, further straining the fragile peace deal struck last week.

US Central Command said aircraft struck missile and drone storage locations and coastal radar sites. CNN, citing an unnamed US official, reported the US operation had concluded. Iranian media said a projectile struck the area around a pier in Sirik in southern Iran.

Elsewhere there were signs of progress, however, as Israel and Lebanon signed an agreement to end the fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Both sides framed the deal as an initial step that calls for Hezbollah to disarm and Israel to withdraw troops from Lebanon, but it was not clear how it would be enforced. Hezbollah said it would not cooperate.

Iran has said it would control the Strait of Hormuz and warned Gulf states not to side with the US after Thursday's attack on a cargo ship travelling near Oman's coast. US President Donald Trump blamed the attack on Iran and said it violated last week's agreement.

"The unwarranted aggression against commercial shipping by Iranian forces clearly violated the ceasefire," US Central Command said in its statement announcing the strikes, which it called "a powerful response to yesterday’s attack on a commercial ship that was transiting the Strait of Hormuz".

The US military said it would continue to provide "safe passage coordination and support" to commercial vessels transiting the strait.

Iranian state media, citing an unnamed military source, reported the strike at the port of Sirik after an explosion was heard there. The source said several warning shots had been fired from Sirik toward vessels that violated Strait of Hormuz regulations about five hours earlier, adding that two warning missiles had also been launched from the nearby Karpan area toward the strategic waterway.

Iran had previously expressed anger at what it said was an "interventionist, irresponsible and provocative" statement by the US and six Gulf states that rejected its assertion that it could charge tolls on vessels transiting the strait.

"Safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz cannot be guaranteed under ambiguous arrangements, parallel routes or decision-making that does not take Iran's role as a coastal state into account," Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on X.

Bloomberg News said Oman, which lies on the opposite side of the strait from Iran, had told allies ships going through Hormuz may have to pay. Reuters could not immediately confirm the report.

title.en: US conducts strikes on Iran after attack on cargo ship
title.zh: 货船遇袭后美国对伊朗实施打击

summary.en: US Central Command says it has struck missile and drone storage facilities and coastal radar positions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US military has conducted strikes on Iranian targets after President Donald Trump accused Iran of a "foolish violation" of its truce following an attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

No casualties were reported when the ship was struck by a one-way attack drone on Thursday, an incident that prompted a planned evacuation of thousands of sailors stuck in the region.

In response, US Central Command said on Friday it had struck missile and drone storage facilities and coastal radar positions. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) blamed the US and Israel.

Just moments before the strikes were announced, Trump said "you'll see" when asked if the US would hit back at Iran.

US Central Command - or Centcom - described the strikes as "a powerful response" to the drone attack.

"The unwarranted aggression against commercial shipping by Iranian forces clearly violated the ceasefire," it said in a statement.

"Furthermore, Iran's dangerous behavior undermined freedom of navigation as commerce increasingly flows through the vital international trade corridor."

Centcom said the US military would "continue to provide safe passage coordination and support to commercial vessels transiting the strait".

For the moment, it is unclear if the US attacks were isolated or form part of a larger, ongoing response.

The IRGC said in a statement later on Friday: "The treaty-breaking US regime as always violated its commitments and launched an airstrike on the coast of the Islamic Republic of Iran under various pretexts of a ship violating an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz."

It added: "If the aggression is repeated our response will be more extensive than this."

The IRGC also accused the "Zionist regime" - a reference to Israel – of violating a ceasefire in Lebanon.

It came as Israel and Lebanon signed a framework agreement for a peace plan in Washington on Friday. Limited fighting has recently continued between Israeli forces and the Iran-backed Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, despite an existing ceasefire.

Tehran effectively closed the strait after US and Israeli attacks against Iran began at the end of February.

The shutdown of the critical waterway for oil and gas shipments caused a spike in global oil prices and choked off shipments of other crucial commodities such as fertiliser.

The US and Iran agreed on 17 June to end hostilities under a 14-point memorandum of understanding, which had also called for Iran to use its "best efforts for the safe passage of commercial vessels with no charge for 60 days".

In a post on X following the US retaliatory strikes, Vice-President JD Vance said that if Iran "has disagreements about how the MOU is being applied, they can pick up the phone".

title.en: Israel and Lebanon sign framework agreement after US-brokered talks
title.zh: 以色列和黎巴嫩在美国斡旋谈判后签署框架协议

summary.en: Israel and Lebanon have signed a framework agreement following US-brokered discussions. This diplomatic step aims to address ongoing tensions, though past ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah have not fully prevented frequent cross-border strikes.
summary.zh: 在由美国斡旋的谈判后，以色列和黎巴嫩签署了一项框架协议。尽管以色列和真主党之间的此前停火未能完全阻止几乎每天的跨境袭击，但此举旨在解决持续的紧张局势。

body.en:
Israel and Lebanon have signed a framework agreement in Washington after several days of negotiations brokered by the US.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the agreement will begin to put in place a framework for lasting peace and security.

It comes as limited fighting has continued between Israeli forces and the Iranian-backed Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, despite an existing ceasefire.

Hezbollah is not party to Friday's agreement, and it is unclear whether it will agree to withdraw its fighters from the South Litani area in southern Lebanon.

Washington has feared that ongoing tension between Israel and Hezbollah could undermine its peace deal with Iran, which includes a commitment to end fighting on "all fronts", including Lebanon.

In the 14-point framework agreement, Israel and Lebanon both "affirm" the right of each state to "live in peace", and express "mutual desire to live in security as neighboring sovereign states".

It makes specific note to a "cessation of all hostile or adverse actions in international political or legal fora" between Israel and Lebanon, with both nations pledging to work towards the release of detainees, as well as the return of any remains.

However, both governments acknowledge that "nothing in this Framework prevents them from exercising their inherent right to defend themselves".

The agreement says that the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) will restore effective sovereign authority over all Lebanese territory, "pending the verified disarmament of non-state armed groups and dismantlement of associated infrastructure".

In order to achieve this, Lebanon makes a specific request for the support of international and "particularly Arab partners, under the leadership of the US".

A US-supported military coordination group will also be established to help implement the framework.

From a diplomatic perspective, the signing of some kind of an agreement is a step forward, but the situation on the ground in Lebanon has shown little sign of shifting, despite several ceasefires.

Israel and Hezbollah have traded cross-border fire, with both accusing each other of violating the agreement, but the intensity has dropped off in recent days.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun said the framework was a first step to restoring sovereignty.

But shortly after the signing, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated that Israeli forces would remain in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah disarms. The Israeli army is currently occupying around 5% of the country's territory.

He said Israel was "allowing the Lebanese army to begin organising to take over some territory" in two pilot zones - one south of the Litani River and another north of it.

BBC reporter Vanessa Silva visited the state of La Guaira in Venezuela, one of the areas worst affected by the twin earthquakes that rocked the country on Wednesday.

title.en: Venezuela earthquakes kill 920 people as families desperate for news
title.zh: 委内瑞拉地震已造成 920 人死亡，家人急于得到消息

summary.en: Hundreds are still feared trapped under the rubble, as international rescue teams start to arrive.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
More than 900 people have been killed and 3,360 others injured in the Venezuela earthquakes, according to the government, as rescuers keep searching for survivors and families wait desperately for news.

The injured are being treated in makeshift medical facilities after dozens of buildings in the country's north were destroyed by the two quakes, including in the capital Caracas.

A senior government official said hundreds of international rescue workers have arrived in the country, with more on the way.

Two powerful earthquakes rocked Venezuela within seconds of each other on Wednesday. The second quake was one of the strongest tremors to hit the country in a century, at a magnitude of 7.5.

La Guaira, a region north of the capital, has been hit the hardest, officials said. The state is also home to one of the country's two main ports and to Simón Bolívar International Airport in Maiquetía - the country's main airport.

Many people are missing, and it is likely the death toll will rise as rescue efforts continue.

In La Guaira, Natacha Diaz told the BBC that her two daughters - aged 22 and 23 - were trapped under the rubble of a collapsed shopping centre, where they worked as manicurists.

"They were with their friends," she said. "I just want them to be found. I have faith and hope that they are there."

National assembly head Jorge Rodriguez said in a state TV broadcast on Friday that the death toll had reached 920, with at least 172 people still believed to be trapped.

In La Guaira alone, at least 243 people have been rescued, the top lawmaker - who is the interim president's brother - said.

Dozens of people have been rescued alive, which "brings us joy that they can embrace their families and loved ones", Acting President Delcy Rodríguez said at a televised briefing on Friday.

Hundreds of buildings have been damaged or destroyed, including a number of hospitals and shopping centres, Jorge Rodríguez said, adding that at least 1,000 other infrastructure sites have also been damaged.

Surviving medical facilities are said to be overwhelmed, with medics telling the BBC that even before the disaster it was difficult to treat patients.

"All our hospitals lack supplies, lack medicines, we are not able to provide medical attention to our people in a normal day," doctor Pedro Javier Fernandez said.

"Now with this tragedy, the emergency is even bigger and it's more difficult to face than in other countries," he added.

There are reports of rescuers pulling people out of collapsed buildings with their bare hands, as disrupted communications, damaged roads, and a lack of resources made the initial emergency response difficult.

body.zh: 据政府称，委内瑞拉地震已造成 900 多人死亡、3,360 人受伤，救援人员仍在继续寻找幸存者，家人则在拼命等待消息。 两次地震摧毁了该国北部的数十座建筑物，其中包括首都加拉加斯，伤者正在临时医疗设施中接受治疗。 一名高级政府官员表示，数百名国际救援人员已抵达该国，还有更多救援人员正在赶来的路上。 周三，委内瑞拉发生了两次强烈地震，几秒钟之内就发生了两次强烈地震。第二次地震是该国一个世纪以来最强烈的地震之一，震级为 7.5 级。 官员们表示，首都以北的拉瓜伊拉地区受到的打击最为严重。该州还拥有该国两个主要港口之一以及该国主要机场迈克蒂亚的西蒙·玻利瓦尔国际机场。 许多人失踪，随着救援工作的继续，死亡人数可能还会上升。 在拉瓜伊拉，娜塔莎·迪亚兹 (Natacha Diaz) 告诉 BBC，她的两个女儿（分别为 22 岁和 23 岁）被困在倒塌购物中心的废墟下，她们在那里做美甲师。 “他们和朋友在一起，”她说。 “我只想找到他们。我有信心并希望他们在那里。” 国民议会议长豪尔赫·罗德里格斯周五在国家电视台播出时表示，死亡人数已达到 920 人，据信至少有 172 人仍被困。 临时总统的弟弟、最高议员表示，仅在拉瓜伊拉就至少有 243 人获救。 代理总统德尔西·罗德里格斯在周五的电视简报会上表示，数十人被生还，这“让我们感到高兴，他们可以拥抱家人和亲人”。 豪尔赫·罗德里格斯说，数百座建筑物遭到破坏或摧毁，其中包括一些医院和购物中心，并补充说至少 1,000 个其他基础设施场所也遭到破坏。 据说幸存的医疗设施已经不堪重负，医护人员告诉英国广播公司，即使在灾难发生之前就很难治疗病人。 佩德罗·哈维尔·费尔南德斯医生说：“我们所有的医院都缺乏物资、药品，我们无法在正常情况下为人民提供医疗服务。” 他补充说：“现在发生了这场悲剧，紧急情况比其他国家更加严重，也更加难以应对。” 据报道，由于通讯中断、道路受损和资源缺乏，救援人员徒手将人们从倒塌的建筑物中救出，这使得最初的应急响应变得困难。 一架载有英国搜救队、警犬和无人机的英国军用飞机于 12 月 17 日离开牛津郡的英国皇家空军布里兹诺顿机场。

summary.en: DW conducted a fact-check on various pieces of disinformation circulating in Europe during a heat wave, including an outdated air-conditioning law, a health myth about sleeping with a fan, and recurring climate change hoax allegations.
summary.zh: 德国之声对欧洲热浪期间流传的各种虚假信息进行了事实核查，其中包括一项过时的空调法律、关于开风扇睡觉的健康谣言以及反复出现的“气候变化骗局”指控。

body.zh: 过时的空调法、开着风扇睡觉的病毒式健康神话以及古老的气候变化骗局指控：德国之声调查了欧洲热浪的传播情况。 本周气温超过 40 摄氏度（104 华氏度），欧洲大部分地区都处于炎热的昏迷状态。 法国遭遇了最严重的天气，周二创下历史最高气温，导致数千户家庭断电。由于居民跳入水中试图降温，已有超过 55 人溺水身亡。 极端天气通常会带来大量虚假信息。这次热浪也不例外。 气候与战略基金会气候虚假信息复原力主管安娜·西维奥雷克(Anna Siewiorek)告诉德国之声，这一信息“必须与人们直接受到影响的事物联系起来”。 “我们感受到热浪，我们感受到风暴或洪水——我们在情感上受到它的影响，因为我们有经济恐惧，我们担心我们所爱的人，我们建造的基础设施等等。” 德国之声事实调查对其中一些虚假和误导性的说法进行了调查。这是冷酷无情的事实。 声称：“西班牙禁止人们将空调温度设置在 27 摄氏度以下，”一位用户在浏览次数超过 80 万次的帖子中写道。 该说法是 2022 年 8 月 3 日撰写的 Time Out 标题的屏幕截图。当时，西班牙政府临时制定了该规则，以应对俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以及由此引发的 2022 年能源危机。 西班牙政府将供暖和制冷温度限制在 19 摄氏度和 27 摄氏度。皇家法令仅适用于公共建筑和商店。一年后就过期了。 当时其他国家也采取了类似的措施：德国强制要求关闭纪念碑周围的灯光，法国对开着空调的商店处以罚款，爱尔兰则拨款资助阁楼和空心墙的隔热。 声称：“开着风扇睡觉是极其危险的，大多数人每晚都会这样做，”另一位用户在一篇被浏览了 170 万次的帖子中写道。这篇文章描述了粉丝如何对你的呼吸系统发起“无声攻击”，蒸发你口腔和鼻子中的水分，使你的眼睛干燥，并导致鼻塞或“剧烈头痛”。 确实，粉丝会让眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴变得干燥，但这种说法被过分夸大了。 世界卫生组织、美国疾病控制与预防中心和英国国家卫生服务中心都建议在酷热时使用电风扇。 同行评审的研究支持了这一点。 《室内空气》(Indoor Air) 上发表的 2019 年睡眠研究发现，老年参与者的睡眠质量同样好——……

reflection.en: In an age of rapid information spread, it is wise to pause and consider the source and veracity of claims, especially during times of public concern. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to be prudent, not gullible, in how we receive and share information.
reflection.zh: 在信息快速传播的时代，尤其是在公众关注的时期，明智的做法是停下来思考信息来源和主张的真实性。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们在接收和分享信息时要谨慎，不要轻信。

verse.textEn: The simple believe anything, but the prudent give thought to their steps.
verse.textZh: 愚蒙人是话都信；通达人步步谨慎。

title.en: 'Operation Purgatory': Magyar moves to demolish Orban system
title.zh: 匈牙利新政府启动“炼狱行动”，着手拆除欧尔班体系

summary.en: The new Hungarian government has initiated "Operation Purgatory" to dismantle the system of former Prime Minister Viktor Orban. The government's stated priorities include combating corruption, reforming the media landscape, and strengthening democratic institutions.
summary.zh: 匈牙利新政府启动“炼狱行动”，迅速着手拆除前总理维克多·欧尔班的体系。此次行动的重点是打击腐败、改革媒体并保护民主。

body.en:
The new Hungarian government is moving swiftly to dismantle the system of former PM Viktor Orban. The focus is on fighting corruption, reforming the media and protecting democracy.

Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar  and his government are setting a fast pace of reform.

In his first few weeks in office, Magyar lifted EU blockades introduced by his predecessor, Viktor Orban , and launched a dialogue with Ukraine , which Orban had labeled "The Empire of Evil."

Back home in Budapest, the parliament approved cuts to the salaries of lawmakers and ministers and limited a prime minister's time in office to a maximum two terms.

But with these changes under his belt, Magyar has now turned his attention to the substance of his predecessor's regime.

Orban had laid plans that stretched decades into the future: In the event of his party losing the election, civil servants who would be difficult to replace would sabotage the work of new governments. In addition, billions had been squirreled away to continue financing Orban's network.

Thanks to a comfortable two-thirds majority in parliament, the government of Magyar and his Tisza party can now dismantle these structures.

In an address to parliament on Monday, Magyar called Orban's style of rule the "mafia system."  He promised to root it out completely using what he called "Operation Purgatory," a name that likely comes from Magyar's penchant for religious and historical symbols.

Magyar has promised that comprehensive investigations will be conducted to establish how Orban's family and friends as well as oligarchs and high-ranking party members lined their pockets and that illegally obtained assets will be recovered.

He has also pledged that state institutions, the judiciary and the media will be reformed in such a way that renders it impossible to return to the Orban system — i.e. to the political control of state institutions and the public.

"Orban wanted to tie the hands of the next ten governments," said the online news outlet 444.hu. "The Magyar administration is now ripping up that plan."

On Tuesday, the parliament passed a first large package of laws relating to "Operation Purgatory."

Most of them were anti-corruption measures. These were key to ensuring that the European Union releases about €17 billion ($19.3 billion) in EU funding for Hungary that was frozen by Brussels because of a perceived risk of corruption during Orban's time in power.

The timing was very important because a deadline for the payment of one large tranche of these funds, some €10.4 billion, passes in August.

One of the most important measures is the abolition of what is known as public interest asset management foundations (KEKVA), private foundations that hold and manage universities, cultural...
body.zh: 匈牙利新政府正在迅速采取行动，废除前总理欧尔班·维克多的制度。重点是打击腐败、改革媒体和保护民主。 匈牙利总理彼得·马扎尔和他的政府正在加快改革步伐。 在上任的头几周内，马扎尔解除了其前任欧尔班·维克多(Viktor Orban)实行的欧盟封锁，并与被欧尔班称为“邪恶帝国”的乌克兰展开对话。 回到布达佩斯，议会批准削减议员和部长的工资，并将总理的任期限制为最多两届。 但随着这些变化，马扎尔现在将注意力转向了前任政权的实质内容。 欧尔班制定了未来几十年的计划：如果他的政党在选举中失败，难以替代的公务员将破坏新政府的工作。此外，还储备了数十亿美元来继续为欧尔班的网络提供资金。 由于在议会中获得了三分之二的多数席位，马扎尔政府和他的蒂萨党现在可以拆除这些结构。 在周一向议会发表的讲话中，马扎尔将欧尔班的统治方式称为“黑手党体系”。 他承诺将通过他所谓的“炼狱行动”彻底根除它，这个名字可能来自马扎尔对宗教和历史符号的偏爱。 马扎尔承诺，将进行全面调查，查明欧尔班的家人和朋友以及寡头和高级党员如何中饱私囊，并追回非法获得的资产。 他还承诺，将对国家机构、司法机构和媒体进行改革，使其不可能回到欧尔班体系，即国家机构和公众的政治控制。 “欧尔班想要束缚接下来十届政府的手脚，”在线新闻媒体 444.hu 说。 “马扎尔政府现在正在撕毁该计划。” 周二，议会通过了第一套与“炼狱行动”相关的大型法律。 其中大部分是反腐败措施。这些对于确保欧盟向匈牙利发放约 170 亿欧元（193 亿美元）的欧盟资金至关重要，这些资金因欧尔班执政期间存在腐败风险而被布鲁塞尔冻结。 这一时机非常重要，因为其中一大笔资金（约 104 亿欧元）的支付截止日期已于 8 月份过去。 最重要的措施之一是废除所谓的公共利益资产管理基金会（KEKVA），即持有和管理大学、文化……的私人基金会。

reflection.en: When leaders prioritize justice and integrity, it brings hope and stability to a nation. The efforts to dismantle corruption and protect democratic principles reflect a commitment to governance that serves the common good. Yahweh's word reminds us that the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the well-being of the people.
reflection.zh: 当领袖们优先考虑公义和廉正时，这会给国家带来希望和稳定。拆除腐败体系和保护民主原则的努力，反映了对服务公共利益的治理的承诺。雅伟的话语提醒我们，掌权者的品格深刻影响着人民的福祉。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: How the Iran war impacts Abu Dhabi's AI strategy
title.zh: 伊朗战争如何影响阿布扎比的人工智能战略

summary.en: Abu Dhabi's ambitions to turn the UAE into a global hub for digital infrastructure and AI, dubbed "UAE AI Strategy 2031," face pressure after the war with Iran. But the UAE is also known for its business resilience.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Abu Dhabi's ambitions to turn the UAE into a global hub for digital infrastructure and AI, dubbed "UAE AI Strategy 2031," face pressure after the war with Iran. But the UAE is also known for its business resilience.

When the United Arab Emirates appointed Omar Sultan Al Olama as the world's first minister of state for Artificial Intelligence in 2017, he promised to turn the UAE into the world's most prepared country for artificial intelligence. Only six years later, Al Olama was listed on TIME magazine's inaugural TIME100 AI list and Abu Dhabi was well underway in implementing its digital strategy .

However, after the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February 2026, the UAE became one of Iran's key targets : Over the course of the war, thousands of Iranian missile and drone strikes were aimed at local offices and data centers operated by global companies such as Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia.

The news magazine The Conversation reported that the war also raised questions about the safety of undersea cables which are essential for data centers and other digital infrastructure. Furthermore, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran , and later by the United States , delayed hardware deliveries.

"Data centers have long become critical infrastructure and need to be better protected just like oil refineries or desalination plants," Sebastian Sons, a senior researcher at the German think tank CARPO, told DW.

Despite the impact of the war on the Gulf state, observers point out that not everything changed. "The political risk profile has changed, but the fundamentals haven't changed," Mohammed Suleiman, a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute in Washington, told DW. "The UAE still lies at the intersection of capital flows between East and West, it still has the energy, land and political will to build AI capabilities at scale," he said.

In the past, the Gulf region has weathered different crises, from the financial crisis of the late 2000s to the COVID-19 pandemic and previous Gulf conflicts, all of which tested the Gulf business model , Sebastian Sons recalls, adding that "during all these crises, the UAE has demonstrated a high level of resilience and found ways to reinvent itself and deal with such strategic situations." In his view, long-term damage would only occur if the Iran conflict continued for a long time and the UAE couldn't find a way to adapt its business model.

However, it remains to be seen in what way the UAE's global compute diplomacy strategy will pivot in the short, medium and long term. In May, a planned $1 billion mega-data-centre project in Kenya was called off, Business Insider Africa reported.

It might as well be that Abu Dhabi's AI strategy is already  diversified enough to withstand the Iran...
body.zh: 阿布扎比将阿联酋打造成全球数字基础设施和人工智能中心的雄心壮志（被称为“阿联酋人工智能战略 2031”）在与伊朗的战争后面临压力。但阿联酋也以其商业弹性而闻名。 2017年，阿拉伯联合酋长国任命奥马尔·苏丹·阿尔·奥拉马为全球首任人工智能国务部长时，他承诺将阿联酋打造成世界上人工智能准备最充分的国家。仅六年后，Al Olama 就被列入《时代》杂志首届 TIME100 AI 榜单，阿布扎比正在顺利实施其数字战略。 然而，在2026年2月美国和以色列袭击伊朗后，阿联酋成为伊朗的关键目标之一：在战争过程中，伊朗数千次导弹和无人机袭击针对亚马逊、谷歌、微软和英伟达等跨国公司运营的当地办事处和数据中心。 新闻杂志《对话》报道称，战争还引发了人们对海底电缆安全性的质疑，而海底电缆对于数据中心和其他数字基础设施至关重要。此外，伊朗以及后来美国对霍尔木兹海峡的封锁导致了硬件交付的延迟。 德国智库 CARPO 高级研究员 Sebastian Sons 告诉德国之声：“数据中心早已成为关键基础设施，需要像炼油厂或海水淡化厂一样得到更好的保护。” 尽管战争对这个海湾国家造成了影响，但观察家指出，一切并没有改变。华盛顿中东研究所高级研究员穆罕默德·苏莱曼对德国之声表示：“政治风险状况已经改变，但基本面没有改变。” “阿联酋仍然位于东西方资本流动的交汇处，它仍然拥有大规模建设人工智能能力的能源、土地和政治意愿，”他说。 过去，海湾地区经历过不同的危机，从2000年代末的金融危机到COVID-19大流行和之前的海湾冲突，所有这些都考验着海湾地区的商业模式，塞巴斯蒂安·桑斯回忆道，他补充说，“在所有这些危机中，阿联酋表现出了高度的韧性，并找到了重塑自身和应对此类战略局势的方法。”他认为，只有伊朗冲突长期持续，而阿联酋又找不到调整其商业模式的方法，才会造成长期损害。 然而，阿联酋的全球计算外交战略在短期、中期和长期将如何转向仍有待观察。据《非洲商业内幕》报道，5 月份，肯尼亚计划耗资 10 亿美元的大型数据中心项目被取消。 阿布扎比的人工智能战略可能已经足够多样化，足以抵御伊朗的攻击……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Bayer: Why so many Roundup weedkiller lawsuits?
title.zh: 拜耳：为何农达除草剂诉讼缠身？

summary.en: Bayer faces numerous lawsuits for allegedly failing to include cancer warnings on its Roundup weedkiller, despite US regulators opposing such a warning. The article questions whether a recent Supreme Court decision will protect the chemical giant from paying billions in damages.
summary.zh: 拜耳公司因被指控未能在其备受争议的农达除草剂上添加癌症警告而面临多起诉讼，尽管美国监管机构反对添加此类警告。德国之声质疑，最近的最高法院裁决是否能阻止这家化工巨头支付数十亿美元的赔偿金。

body.en:
Bayer was sued for failing to add cancer warnings to its controversial pesticide Roundup when US regulators opposed adding one. DW asks if the latest Supreme Court win will shield the chemical giant from paying billions.

Bayer is still grappling with tens of thousands of lawsuits over its glyphosate -based weedkiller Roundup, which plaintiffs claim causes cancer , primarily non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

Germany's agrochemicals giant inherited the legal mess after taking over Monsanto, the company that produced Roundup, in 2018.

Farmers, landscapers and gardeners — mostly based in the United States — argue that Monsanto knew, or should have known, about the risks but failed to provide adequate warnings on product labels.

According to the Lawsuit Information Center, Bayer has so far paid out around $11 billion (€9.65 billion) to settle roughly 100,000 cases. Around 61,000 to 65,000 claims remain active.

The company has cited decades of scientific studies and regulatory research showing that glyphosate is safe and does not cause cancer.

Bayer, which is among the top firms listed on the Frankfurt stock exchange, has won several legal cases, but it has also been hit with several high‑profile losses.

On Thursday, the top US court delivered a major victory to Bayer , ruling that claimants cannot sue the company in state courts over the lack of cancer warnings on the weedkiller.

The justices decided 7-2 that, as US federal regulators do not require a warning on products containing glyphosate, individual states cannot force companies to add one.

The case centered on a gardener, John Durnell from St Louis, Missouri, who won $1.25 million in compensation after blaming Roundup for his cancer.

The Supreme Court, however, ruled Thursday that Federal law, which governs pesticides, takes priority.

Durnell’s lawsuit became the key test case for thousands of other claims in state courts, even though the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had signed off on Roundup's labels.

In 2019, the EPA wrote to glyphosate producers telling them that adding a cancer warning would be "false and misleading."

This effectively barred Bayer from adding the warning, even when required to by state regulators.

The company, which is headquartered in Leverkusen, western Germany, argued it should not be punished for following federal rules.

In a statement after the Supreme Court ruling, Bayer said that glyphosate remains the "most studied crop protection tool in the world," adding that the decision "affirms that the EPA’s safety determination is the law of the land."

No. This latest ruling removes just one key type of claim against Bayer, specifically failing to follow state laws and add a cancer...
body.zh: 拜耳因未能在其备受争议的农药农达中添加癌症警告而被起诉，而美国监管机构反对添加这一警告。德国之声询问最高法院最新的胜诉是否会阻止这家化学巨头支付数十亿美元。 拜耳仍在努力应对数万起有关其基于草甘膦的除草剂农达的诉讼，原告声称该产品会导致癌症，主要是非霍奇金淋巴瘤。 德国农化巨头在 2018 年收购了生产农达的孟山都公司后，接手了法律上的混乱局面。 农民、园林设计师和园丁（主要来自美国）认为孟山都公司知道或应该知道这些风险，但未能在产品标签上提供足够的警告。 据诉讼信息中心称，拜耳迄今已支付约 110 亿美元（96.5 亿欧元）来解决约 10 万起案件。大约 61,000 至 65,000 份索赔仍然有效。 该公司引用了数十年的科学研究和监管研究表明草甘膦是安全的并且不会致癌。 拜耳是法兰克福证券交易所顶级上市公司之一，已赢得多起法律诉讼，但也遭受了多起引人注目的损失。 周四，美国最高法院为拜耳带来了重大胜利，裁定原告不能因该除草剂缺乏癌症警告而在州法院起诉该公司。 法官以 7-2 的方式裁定，由于美国联邦监管机构不要求对含有草甘膦的产品发出警告，因此各个州不能强迫公司添加警告。 此案以来自密苏里州圣路易斯的园丁 John Durnell 为中心，他在将癌症归咎于农达后获得了 125 万美元的赔偿。 然而，最高法院周四裁定，管理农药的联邦法律优先。 尽管美国环境保护署 (EPA) 已经批准了农达的标签，但德内尔的诉讼成为州法院数千起其他索赔的关键测试案例。 2019 年，美国环保局写信给草甘膦生产商，告诉他们添加癌症警告将是“虚假和误导性的”。 这实际上阻止了拜耳添加警告，即使州监管机构要求这样做。 该公司总部位于德国西部勒沃库森，辩称它不应因遵守联邦规则而受到惩罚。 在最高法院裁决后的一份声明中，拜耳表示，草甘膦仍然是“世界上研究最多的作物保护工具”，并补充说，该裁决“确认了美国环保局的安全决定是国家法律”。 不。这项最新裁决仅删除了针对拜耳的一项关键索赔，特别是未能遵守州法律并增加了癌症......

reflection.en: The ongoing legal battles surrounding Roundup highlight the critical importance of honesty and transparency in commerce. Yahweh delights in integrity, and this story reminds us that businesses bear a profound responsibility to provide accurate information about their products, especially concerning public health.

body.en:
King Charles has revealed that he paid £12.9 million (more than $24.6 million) in tax last year, marking the first time a monarch has publicly disclosed how much personal tax he paid.

That places Charles among the UK's top 100 taxpayers between 2024-2025, local media reported.

The monarch is not liable for tax, but his mother, Queen Elizabeth, began paying it voluntarily in 1993.

Buckingham Palace described the landmark disclosure as part of its "commitment to transparency". Royal finances have long been considered complex, murky and difficult to decipher, and the latest disclosure — which did not include breakdowns of how the figures were calculated — does little to lift the veil.

Royal finances have come under increasing scrutiny in recent years, including following a recent watchdog report into property arrangements involving the king's brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

Palace officials said the amount of tax payable by Charles since he became king in 2022 exceeded £30 million ($57 million).

That includes more than £11.7 million ($22 million) of tax paid from 2023-2024.

The figure for the year following Queen Elizabeth's death in September 2022 was not provided. Tax years in Britain run from early April.

Charles had previously disclosed the amount of tax he paid prior to becoming monarch.

In a similar move, Charles' eldest son, Prince William, also released his personal tax information. The royal report detailed that William paid more than £7.7 million ($14.75 million) in income and capital gain taxes in 2024-2025. The year prior, he paid £8.3 million ($15.9 million), according to his office.

That includes the Sovereign Grant, which provides official public funding for the monarchy and the Privy Purse, which supplies Charles' income through revenue generated by the Duchy of Lancaster estate.

In 2025-2026, funding for the Sovereign Grant increased to £132.1 million (more than $253 million).

Charles receives personal income from land, private estates and investments on top of that figure, which he receives from the government to support royal duties.

Charles' private sources of income include his Balmoral and Sandringham estates as well as art, jewellery, stamp collections, investments and private savings.

In a palace statement published on Thursday, James Chalmers, the Charles' treasurer and keeper of the privy purse, said: "While Royal finances can sometimes appear complex, the underlying system is clear in principle, structured in law and refined over time to ensure the Monarch can serve with independence, accountability and in the...

body.en:
Australians have been caught up in the devastating earthquakes that hit Venezuela on Thursday.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has confirmed that it is providing consular support "to a small number of Australians that have been affected by the earthquake in Venezuela".

"Owing to our privacy obligations we are unable to provide further comment on individual cases," a spokesperson told SBS News in a statement. They did not confirm in what capacity those citizens have been impacted.

Australian officials are in close contact with local authorities, government, and partners who are attempting to rescue those trapped under the rubble.

Australia does not have an embassy in Venezuela, and the government's ability to provide consular assistance is severely limited.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Friday that his heart "goes out" to anyone with relatives or friends in the country who have been affected by the natural disasters that struck the country's north on Thursday .

"This is one of the worst earthquakes that we've seen in recent times, with catastrophic human consequences, a massive loss of life, but also massive infrastructure damage and real consequences for the people of Venezuela," the prime minister told ABC News Breakfast.

Genesis Lindstrom, president of the Venezuelan Association of Australia, has her community has been desperately seeking information, which is challenging to access given the number of media outlets suspended in the country.

"A lot of the news and updates we're getting are from social media and from people sending through videos and updates," she told News Breakfast.

Lindstrom added that she was in the office when the news broke and started frantically messaging everyone she knows in the country's capital, Caracas.

"Thankfully, as far as I know, most people in my community here have been getting those messages across from family members and loved ones," she said.

Desperate Venezuelans are continuing to dig for people trapped beneath the debris in the worst-hit state of La Guaira, north of Caracas.

The United States Geological Survey measured the earthquakes as magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, which struck within minutes of each other on Thursday.

Venezuela's health minister Carlos Alvarado said the death toll had risen to 235. At least 1,520 are thought to be injured.

The United Nation's Central Emergency Response Fund has released $22 million to support response efforts in Venezuela.

United Nations-certified rescuers will help search for survivors, interim Venezuelan president Delcy Rodriguez said in a televised message.

body.en:
It's been a big day for football fans in Australia, with the Socceroos' make-or-break match against Paraguay ending nil-all — securing Australia's spot in the Round of 32.

The 0-0 result was enough for the Socceroos to finish second in Group D, allowing them to advance to the knockouts for the third time in history. There, they'll face the second-placed Group G team — whoever they turn out to be — on 4 July at 4am AEST.

The Socceroos, who defeated Türkiye in their opening match before losing to the United States, were never seriously threatened on their way to securing a point to reach the last 32.

title.en: The 'yellow line' Gazans have been killed for crossing, according to new report
title.zh: 新报告称，加沙人因越过“黄线”而被杀害

summary.en: A new report indicates that children in Gaza continue to be targeted even after a ceasefire, a finding that Israel has rejected.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，即使在停火之后，加沙的儿童仍被当作目标，以色列对此调查结果表示拒绝。

body.en:
Eight months after the Gaza ceasefire began , Palestinian children are still being targeted by Israeli forces for crossing the vaguely defined "yellow line", according to a new report from the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry.

The commission alleges Israeli forces have continued to deliberately target Palestinian children during the ceasefire, which, alongside the targeting of healthcare and education facilities and restricting the flow of aid, it says is severely impacting the ability of children to thrive.

"Even if the bombs and guns fall silent in Gaza and the West Bank, Palestinian children will not simply recover overnight," the commission's chair, Srinivasan Muralidhar, said in a statement.

The United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry, which does not speak on behalf of the UN as a whole and has been sharply criticised by Israel, concluded in September that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Israel is separately defending a genocide case at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), which has ordered provisional measures but has yet to issue a final ruling.

A spokesperson for Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs rejected the recent report's findings, calling it a "propaganda piece as outrageous as its previous ones".

"It completely erases Israeli children who were brutally murdered, kidnapped, and targeted by Hamas, while ignoring Hamas' cynical use of Palestinian children as human shields and pawns of war," it said.

Since the ceasefire began in October, the Ministry of Health in Gaza reported that at least 978 Palestinians had been killed, and just under 4,000 injured — a statistic that cannot be independently verified as Israel does not permit international journalists to enter Gaza.

The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) estimated 265 of post-ceasefire deaths were children.

Israel and Hamas have repeatedly accused each other of violating the truce since it came into effect.

Australian emergency doctor Thienminh Dinh, 37, managed medical activities at the Doctors Without Borders field hospital in Al-Zawaida, Gaza, for two stints.

The first, between May and June 2025, was before the ceasefire. The second stint, between October and December 2025, began shortly after the ceasefire was announced.

She told SBS News there was a slight decrease in the volume of air strikes after the ceasefire, but the attacks still continued.

title.en: Debris falls after plane hits Beijing's tallest building
title.zh: 飞机撞上北京第一高楼 碎片掉落

summary.en: Social media footage showed the moment debris from a small aircraft fell to the ground after a crash into Beijing's tallest skyscraper.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Video shows the moment debris from a small aircraft fell to the ground after a crash into Beijing's tallest skyscraper.

Eyewitnesses told Reuters news agency that an aircraft the size of a car crashed into the CITIC Tower, also known as China Zun, on Friday.

Social media footage captured from a building nearby showed what appeared to be a small plane on the ground. Firefighters were also seen extinguishing a fire in the tower.

CITIC Tower is a 108-storey skyscraper in Beijing's central business district and the headquarters of the state-owned conglomerate CITIC Group, one of China's largest.

It is not known if there were any casualties and there has been no immediate comment from authorities about the incident.
body.zh: 视频显示一架小型飞机撞上北京最高摩天大楼后残骸掉落地面的瞬间。 目击者告诉路透社，周五，一架汽车大小的飞机撞上了中信大厦（也称为“中国尊”）。 从附近一座建筑物捕捉到的社交媒体视频显示，地面上似乎有一架小型飞机。人们还看到消防队员正在扑灭塔内的大火。 中信大厦是北京中央商务区的一座 108 层摩天大楼，也是中国最大的国有企业集团之一的中信集团的总部。 目前尚不清楚是否有人员伤亡，当局也没有立即对这一事件发表评论。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to truth, discernment, and honest speech. Philippians 4:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with discernment and truthful speech, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到真理、分辨与诚实。Philippians 4:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以分辨与诚实表达来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: Weather tracker: Heatwave expected to bring Germany and Poland to 40C
title.zh: 天气追踪：德国和波兰预计将迎来40摄氏度高温热浪

summary.en: An intense heatwave is expected to bring temperatures up to 40C in parts of central and northern Europe, including Germany and Poland. The Austrian Grand Prix has declared a heat hazard due to the dramatic rise in temperatures.
summary.zh: 预计一股强烈的热浪将使中欧和北欧部分地区（包括德国和波兰）的气温升至40摄氏度。由于气温急剧上升，奥地利大奖赛已宣布高温危险。

body.en: Austrian Grand Prix declares heat hazard as dramatic rise in temperatures forecast in central and northern Europe Temperatures are forecast to rise dramatically in parts of central and northern Europe this weekend as the intense heatwave continues . In Germany and Poland, highs up to or exceeding 40C (104F) are expected on both Saturday and Sunday, days after swathes of France experienced similar extreme temperatures. The Austrian Grand Prix, taking place this weekend in Spielberg, has declared a heat hazard , the first race to do so this season. Temperatures are expected to rise into the low 30s celsius during the race, almost 10C warmer than usual for the venue. Across Europe, the intense heat has led to severe thunderstorms. In the Sverdlovsk region of central Russia, a strong tornado was reported on the evening of 22 June. Rated a 3 out of 5 on the international Fujita scale, the twister injured 16 people and destroyed or damaged about 100 homes and businesses in the town of Kushva. Emergency services have been working on restoring power to the town. Tornadoes are not unheard of in Russia but are rare. Forecasters say they may become more common in future as the climate breaks down. Storm warnings remained in effect in the southern part of the country on Friday. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The dramatic rise in temperatures across Europe reminds us that creation itself is experiencing distress. As the natural world groans under changing conditions, we are called to reflect on our interconnectedness with the earth and its well-being. This intense heatwave serves as a poignant reminder of the broader challenges facing our shared home.
reflection.zh: 欧洲气温的急剧上升提醒我们，受造界本身正在经历痛苦。当自然界在不断变化的环境下发出呻吟时，我们被呼召反思我们与地球及其福祉的相互关联。这场强烈热浪是对我们共同家园所面临的更广泛挑战的深刻提醒。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Southeast Asia boost defense ties but avoids firm alliances
title.zh: 东南亚加强防务关系但避免建立牢固联盟

summary.en: Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.
summary.zh: 东南亚各国正在扩大防务合作，这改变了南海局势，但尚未形成新的反华联盟。

body.en:
Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.

For years, the South China Sea has been seen as a potential flashpoint in the intensifying geopolitical rivalry between China and the United States.   

Southeast Asian states are often presented as the smaller powers caught in the storm.

That picture is changing, however, as a new and subtle security network takes shape across the region.

It's built not around formal alliances but around access deals, missile sales, coast guard drills, intelligence-sharing talks and defense consultations.

On June 1, the Philippines and Vietnam upgraded ties to an enhanced strategic partnership and signed a memorandum on defense cooperation which commits them to high-level exchanges, strategic dialogue, information sharing and joint activities at sea.

The partnership builds on earlier coast guard arrangements, including a hotline and mechanisms to prevent incidents.

Late last month, Indian officials said that New Delhi had signed a $629 million (€555 million) deal to supply Vietnam with the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system.

Vietnam is the second Southeast Asian buyer publicly confirmed by India, after the Philippines, which signed a $375 million contract in 2022 for three BrahMos batteries. The missiles are jointly developed by India and Russia.

Meanwhile, Japan's security relationship with the Philippines has grown quite concrete.   A Reciprocal Access Agreement entered into force last September , expanding troop deployment in each country, while this month they began talks over a new deal to share classified defense information.

In February, Australia and Indonesia signed the "Jakarta Treaty," a common security pact that commits the two governments to regular top-level consultations.

None of these agreements creates a NATO-style alliance . Together, however, they show how middle powers are trying to make unilateral pressure at sea harder and costlier.

All these countries share concerns about China and an interest in upholding the rule of law at sea and keeping the region free from coercion by great powers, Hunter Marston, director of the Southeast Asia Program at the Lowy Institute, told DW.

At the same time, they recognize — to varying degrees — the possibility that the US could scale back its commitments to regional security, which would introduce volatility and unpredictability into the prevailing balance of power, he said.

"While they don't all see eye to eye on regional security or support the United States military presence equally, now is the time for middle powers to band together to stand up for their interests. None are strong enough to do so...
body.zh: 该地区各国正在扩大防务合作，其方式改变了南海局势，但并未形成新的反华集团。 多年来，南海一直被视为中美地缘政治竞争的潜在爆发点。 东南亚国家经常被描述为陷入风暴的小国。 然而，随着整个地区新的、微妙的安全网络的形成，这种情况正在发生变化。 它不是围绕正式联盟建立的，而是围绕准入协议、导弹销售、海岸警卫队演习、情报共享会谈和国防磋商建立的。 6 月 1 日，菲律宾和越南将关系提升为强化战略伙伴关系，并签署了一份防务合作备忘录，承诺两国进行高层交往、战略对话、信息共享和海上联合活动。 该伙伴关系建立在早期海岸警卫队安排的基础上，包括热线电话和预防事件的机制。 上个月末，印度官员表示，新德里已签署一项价值 6.29 亿美元（5.55 亿欧元）的协议，向越南提供布拉莫斯超音速巡航导弹系统。 越南是继菲律宾之后印度公开确认的第二个东南亚买家，菲律宾于2022年签署了价值3.75亿美元的三块布拉莫斯电池合同。该导弹由印度和俄罗斯联合研制。 与此同时，日本与菲律宾的安全关系变得相当具体。 去年九月，一项互惠访问协议生效，扩大了两国的部队部署，本月他们开始就一项共享机密国防信息的新协议进行谈判。 今年二月，澳大利亚和印度尼西亚签署了《雅加达条约》，这是一项共同安全条约，要求两国政府定期进行高层磋商。 这些协议都没有创建北约式的联盟。然而，它们共同表明中等强国如何试图加大海上单边施压的难度和成本。 洛伊研究所东南亚项目主任亨特·马斯顿告诉德国之声，所有这些国家都对中国感到担忧，都对维护海上法治和使该地区免受大国胁迫感兴趣。 他表示，与此同时，他们在不同程度上认识到美国可能缩减其对地区安全的承诺，这将给当前的均势带来波动和不可预测性。 “虽然他们在地区安全问题上意见不一，也并不平等地支持美国的军事存在，但现在是中等强国联合起来维护自身利益的时候了。没有一个国家足够强大，可以这样做……

reflection.en: The nations of Southeast Asia are navigating complex geopolitical waters, seeking security through cooperation while carefully avoiding actions that could escalate tensions. This delicate balance reflects a desire to live at peace, as far as it depends on them, even amidst strategic disagreements. Yahweh calls us to pursue peace with all people, a principle...
reflection.zh: 东南亚各国在复杂的国际局势中寻求平衡，通过防务合作增强安全，同时谨慎避免可能加剧紧张局势的行动。这种微妙的平衡反映了他们尽力与各方和平相处的愿望，即使存在战略分歧。雅伟呼召我们尽力与所有人和睦相处，这一原则指导着人际关系和国际外交。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Dear You review – enjoyable Chinese romdram crosses generations as it tracks down a missing husband
title.zh: 《亲爱的你》影评：一部跨越世代、追寻失踪丈夫的感人华语爱情剧情片

summary.en: The Guardian China reviews "Dear You," a Chinese romantic drama by director Lan Hongchun. The film is a multi-generational family saga, spanning from the 1940s to the present, primarily set in Bangkok, and follows the search for a husband who disappeared in Thailand.
summary.zh: 《卫报中国》评论了导演蓝鸿春的华语爱情剧情片《亲爱的你》。这部电影是一部跨越几代人的家族传奇，故事从20世纪40年代至今，主要背景设在曼谷，讲述了一个家庭寻找在泰国失踪的丈夫的故事。

body.en: Director Lan Hongchun’s family saga feels like a good old-fashioned novel as it goes in search of a man who has disappeared in Thailand With a story that ranges from the 1940s to the present and, although mostly set in Bangkok, revolving largely around Teochew-speaking Chinese from Guangdong, this generations-spanning drama feels like a good old-fashioned novel. A romantic beach read, perhaps, the kind in which coincidences and random accidents cause misunderstandings that last for decades until the truth is finally revealed. It’s sentimental in places, sure, but there’s also a fair bit of salty, bawdy humour to cut the sweetness, lashings of period colour, and impressively naturalistic performances from a mostly non-professional cast. All that has helped to make this an unexpectedly large box-office hit in the People’s Republic last month; and for non-Chinese or Thai rom-dram aficionados anywhere, it’s well worth looking out for. As the story opens in the 21st century in the Chinese city of Shantou, octogenarian Shurou (Iap Sok-jiu) is celebrating her 87th birthday, surrounded by adoring friends, family and neighbours who revere the matriarch, not least for managing to raise three kids on her own in the 1940s and 50s. Her shifty grandson Xiaowei (Hiau-ui), however, is less of a solid citizen and, having got into debt, he decides to travel to Bangkok to find out if Shurou’s husband Zheng Musheng, not seen for decades, could help out since he’s reputed to have made a fortune out there, endowed schools all over Thailand, and had a second family after abandoning Shurou. Continue reading...
body.zh: 导演兰鸿春的家庭传奇感觉就像一部优秀的老式小说，讲述了在泰国寻找失踪男子的故事。故事范围从 20 世纪 40 年代至今，虽然主要以曼谷为背景，但主要围绕来自广东的潮州华人展开，这部跨越几代人的戏剧感觉就像一部优秀的老式小说。浪漫的海滩读物，也许是那种巧合和偶然的事故会导致持续数十年的误会，直到真相最终揭晓的类型。当然，它在某些地方是感伤的，但也有一些咸味、下流的幽默来削弱甜蜜，充满时代色彩，以及来自大多数非专业演员的令人印象深刻的自然主义表演。所有这些都使得该片上个月在中华人民共和国取得了意想不到的票房大成功。对于任何地方的非中国或泰国的浪漫剧爱好者来说，这都非常值得一看。故事发生在 21 世纪的中国汕头市，八十多岁的淑柔（叶淑如饰）正在庆祝她的 87 岁生日，周围都是崇拜这位女族长的朋友、家人和邻居，尤其是她在 20 世纪 40 年代和 50 年代设法独自抚养三个孩子。然而，她狡猾的孙子小伟（孝仪饰）却不是一个踏实的公民，负债累累，他决定前往曼谷，看看书柔数十年未见的丈夫郑木胜是否可以帮忙，因为他在外面发了大财，为泰国各地的学校捐款，并在抛弃书柔后有了第二个家庭。继续阅读...

This long quest reflects the deep commitment inherent in marriage, where two become one, a union that transcends time and distance. It reminds us that true connection often calls for steadfastness, even in the face of profound...

title.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
title.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英获德国之声表彰

summary.en: Jimmy Lai, a Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher, has been honored by DW. He founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper before being sentenced to 20 years in prison. His son stated that the award signifies that those who advocate for the freedom of others are not alone.
summary.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英获得德国之声表彰。他在被判处20年监禁前，创办了香港最大的亲民主报纸。他的儿子表示，这个奖项表明那些为他人自由而奋斗的人“从不孤单”。

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent more than 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW honored Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award  at the annual Global Media Forum in Bonn, Germany, on Tuesday.

"While we have spoken freely in the defence of independent media, Jimmy, who founded an independent media company because he believed in the rights of the Hong Kong people to receive information, is locked away for those beliefs," Jodie Ginsberg, CEO of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a speech honoring Lai.

"The attacks on Apple Daily and its counterparts in Hong Kong presaged the far greater attacks on civil liberties in the years that followed. Jimmy Lai saw this and spoke out. We can honor him today not only by fighting for his freedom, but by defending the freedoms for which he was jailed."

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

title.en: The hidden pollution stealing our view of the universe
title.zh: 隐藏的污染偷走了我们对宇宙的看法

summary.en: As the night sky grows brighter, some Australians are fighting to save what's disappearing from above them.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Kai Lane says the last thing he sees before he settles in for sleep is the stars — or at least what's left of them.

For the 24-year-old Yorta Yorta and Barapa Barapa man, the night sky has become both a memory and a warning. A reminder of what's at stake, as artificial light erases the stars above many Australian towns and cities.

"I never shut my curtains … I sort of lay on the side and look out the window and up at the stars. Then I slowly doze off," Lane tells SBS News.

Across Australia, scientists and ecologists increasingly say that light pollution is not just a loss of scenery.

It's a cultural and ecological shift, altering ecosystems, wildlife behaviours, and in some cases, obscuring First Nations knowledge systems that have relied on the night sky for tens of thousands of years.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Lane was raised in Kerang, in north-central Victoria, where the clear night sky reveals dense constellations. He describes this nightscape as a "living classroom", where stories are encoded in darkness just as much as light.

Among them is Emu in the Sky, an Indigenous constellation traced through the dark patches of the Milky Way rather than its stars.

"We are the only culture in the world that looks for dark spots in the Milky Way. Usually, the constellations are just connecting stars to stars, like lines. But the emu is just a dark spot in the sky," Lane says.

For the Barapa Barapa people, the constellation carries practical lessons as well as cultural meaning. Lane says the emu's position can signal when it's appropriate to collect eggs or when breeding season has begun.

"When it's sitting down, you can go collect the eggs, and when the emu starts to stand, you're not allowed to crack the eggs because they're starting to become chicks."

Lane is also a trainee ecologist and says these stories reveal deeper lessons about connection to Country, seasons and ecological change.

But he believes this knowledge is under threat , as artificial light increasingly brightens city centres, parts of regional and rural Australia alike.

Lane now lives in the Victorian city of Geelong, where only a handful of stars are visible on a clear night.

It's a sight familiar to many Australians who live under light pollution — the excessive or inappropriate use of artificial light at night. One form of light pollution is skyglow, in which artificial lighting brightens the night sky and reduces the visibility of celestial objects.

body.en:
Fans decked out in green and gold turned out across the country to support the Socceroos as they drew with Paraguay to secure a spot in the World Cup knockout rounds.

And the Socceroos said they felt the love, when shown footage by SBS reporters of children at an Australian primary school erupting at the end of the match.

"It gives you a bit of self satisfaction that we have put a smile on all these people's faces and our journey isn't over yet so hopefully we can continue our journey for as long as possible."

Rowdy crowds packed Melbourne's Federation Square, pushing it to maximum capacity by 10am. Multiple flares were let off and a small brawl broke out but the atmosphere was mostly positive, if charged.

Roughly 7,500 people packed into the live site to watch the match, which resulted in a 0-0 draw — but was sufficient to send Australia through to the knockout round of the tournament.

While the fan base was a mixture of ages, teenagers who should have been at school for the last day of term filled Fed Square, some wearing the Australian flag as a cape.

Chants of "Aussie, Aussie, Aussie" could be heard through the crowd while beach balls were bounced over the audience.

Ducking responsibilities to support the national team was a bit of a theme on Friday, given the 12pm AEST kick- off.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he expected employers would be understanding if staff failed to return to work after lunch if the Socceroos won, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said bosses should act "with thoughts of our national interest".

Two unnamed fans told SBS News at Fed Square during the match: "It's un-Australian not to take the sick leave to get it off."

At Sydney's main viewing site, Tumbalong Park, similar numbers were seen, with many fans also on the younger side.

"I’m missing school. It's the last day of term for us, but you gotta support the Socceroos," a fan told SBS News.

While most fans were well behaved, three teenagers in Melbourne were issued penalty notices for riotous behaviour and given move-on notices. In Sydney, a 16-year-old was arrested at Tumbalong Park.

Australia managed to secure a convincing entry to the round of 32 with their clean sheet draw with Paraguay. They will face off against the second-placed team from Group G on 4 July.

Both major party leaders congratulated the team, with Opposition leader Angus Taylor referencing his famous digital blunder to congratulate the Socceroos. In 2019, he replied to his own Facebook post about extra car parking spaces at NSW railway stations with the comment: Fantastic. Great move. Well done Angus.

title.en: Melbourne beach temporarily renamed after Patrick Beach as Socceroos reach Round of 32
title.zh: 墨尔本海滩因足球队门将帕特里克·比奇表现出色而暂时更名

summary.en: Socceroos goalkeeper Patrick Beach's performance in the team's match against Paraguay has earned him a tribute back in Melbourne, with a local beach temporarily renamed in his honor.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚足球队门将帕特里克·比奇在对阵巴拉圭的比赛中表现出色，墨尔本的一处海滩因此暂时以他的名字命名，以示敬意。

body.en:
The City of Port Philip in Melbourne's south says the iconic beachfront will be renamed after Melbourne City and Socceroos goalkeeper Patrick Beach for the remainder of the national squad's FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign.

It comes after the team's 0-0 draw against Paraguay secured their spot in the knockout rounds of this year's tournament.

At 22 years old, the goalkeeper made a surprise World Cup debut for the Socceroos against Türkiye and has remained in goal for all of the side's 2026 World Cup games.

He saved two shots on target in the Socceroos' clash against Paraguay and is one of seven players on the squad with Melbourne City connections.

Melbourne City FC CEO Brad Rowse said his side was "incredibly proud" of the young player.

"You spend years developing players and hope they make a World Cup squad," Rowse said.

"Having a beach renamed after one of them wasn't something we'd planned for, but we're happy to take it."

The council's town hall will also be illuminated in green and gold on Friday night, following the team's third-ever entry into the knockout round.

City of Port Phillip mayor Alex Makin said his council wanted to celebrate the Socceroos' win and the strong connection between Melbourne and the national squad.

"This is about getting behind the Socceroos and sharing in the excitement of the World Cup at home," he said in a statement.

"Renaming St Kilda Beach is a uniquely local way to celebrate the team and embrace the global energy right here in Port Phillip.”

The City of Port Philip said plans for a mural dedicated to the young player were "underway".

Having made it through to the Round of 32, Australia will next face the second-placed Group G team on 4 July in Arlington, Texas.

title.en: Karl Stefanovic exits Nine Network after controversial podcast interview
title.zh: 卡尔·斯特凡诺维奇因争议播客采访退出九号电视网

summary.en: Veteran Today host Karl Stefanovic will depart the Nine Network immediately, the network announced. Stefanovic later stated in a video that he was "free."
summary.zh: 九号电视网宣布，资深《今日》节目主持人卡尔·斯特凡诺维奇将立即离职。斯特凡诺维奇随后在一段视频中表示他“自由了”。

body.en:
Karl Stefanovic will leave Nine after nearly two decades on the Today show, following a podcast interview with far-right British figure Tommy Robinson.

Nine chief executive Matt Stanton informed staff in an email on Friday that it was the "right time" for Stefanovic to move on, the Sydney Morning Herald — owned by Nine — reported.

"Karl has been a fixture on our screens for over two decades, so we know this is a significant change for our viewers and all of us here at Nine, however it’s the right time to make it," Stanton said in the email.

In a statement to SBS News, Nine said Stefanovic was already set to leave the network at the end of the year.

"Nine Entertainment and Karl Stefanovic have agreed that it is no longer possible for him to continue hosting Today at the same time as his independent podcast," a spokesperson told SBS News.

"While Karl and Nine had previously agreed he would leave Today at the end of this year, they have subsequently decided he will leave the Network immediately."

Executives finalised the terms of his exit on Friday morning, ending his run as Australia's highest-paid television presenter.

It remains unclear whether Nine will pay out the estimated $1 million balance of his contract.

On Friday morning, Stefanovic released a statement via a YouTube video, saying he was "free".

"I’m free. Truly independent. I didn’t get the chance to thank my free-to-air audience for 21 years, so thank you for riding the ups and downs," he said.

"It wasn’t easy, this last couple of days, but we rolled on. So here’s what I believe in: the public deserve to hear perspectives."

"On my show, I’ve spoken to people who have different perspectives — I know that winds some people up.

"Sometimes I agree with everything a guest says, sometimes I don’t. But importantly, you get to make up your mind."

"Freedom of speech — here and around the world — is what this show is about. You don’t have to listen to my show — you have the power."

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who has previously been a guest on Stefanovic's show, said the situation was "unfortunate" but that "words do matter".

"It’s a matter, of course, for Channel Nine, but words do matter, and what people who are very prominent in our public discourse do, and how they conduct themselves, matters as well," Albanese told ABC.

"It’s unfortunate — the way that what has been a very big career has ended in this way — but that’s a matter for Karl Stefanovic, to think about his actions and the decisions that he’s...

title.en: Sickies, long lunches, green-and-gold fever: Australia set for a midday Socceroos party

summary.en: With the Socceroos one match away from the World Cup knockout rounds, employers are being urged to embrace football fever.

body.en:
Australia's big FIFA World Cup clash against Paraguay is expected to bring workplaces across the country to a standstill, with pubs, live sites and office watch parties set to fill as millions tune in.

Employers are also bracing for a spike in sickies and work-from-home requests as the Socceroos look to seal their place in the Round of 32 in their final group match, and first fixture that falls squarely in the middle of the workday (12pm Friday AEST). You can watch it live and free on SBS or SBS On Demand.

The stakes are high. A win or draw will send Australia through, while defeat could either end the Socceroos' campaign or leave them facing a tougher opponent in the knockout rounds.

As former prime minister Bob Hawke famously said after Australia won the America's Cup in 1983: "Any boss who sacks anyone for not turning up today is a bum."

While Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hasn't gone that far, he has encouraged employers to treat any workers watching the Socceroos "kindly" and "with thoughts of our national interest".

"I know that Australian workers will be, of course, very passionate about the Socceroos — and I know that Australian employers will be generous in their approach to these things," he told ABC News Breakfast.

Albanese added that his morning meetings will also be finishing earlier so his team can watch the game.

"I've got a Ministry meeting here in Parliament House this morning. It will end sharply at 11:30am, I assure you, so that people can get in front of their TV screen and watch it on SBS."

"It will be a great couple of hours. I'm sure the whole of Australia will be cheering on the Socceroos."

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he thought employers would "understand" if workers didn't return to the office, should the Socceroos win.

"I suspect there might be a few long-ish lunches, particularly if we win," he told reporters in Canberra on Friday morning.

"I think a lot of people might be finding a reason not to go back to the office after lunch if we win, and you know, that's a good thing."

"I think a lot of employers around the country would understand if people don't come back on site or back to the office after lunch, if we win."

Nearly five million Australians tuned in for the Socceroos' opening match against Türkiye , while more than 3.4 million set their alarms early to watch them take on the USA.

A similar figure is expected today for the midday clash, with many workers to be glued to their phones or crowded around lunchroom screens.
